**Depreciation of a $60 000 asset Salvage value = $10 000 Useful life = 5 years US GAAP** | Year | Straight‑Line Expense | SL Accumulated Dep. | SL Book Value | |------|-----------------------|---------------------|---------------| | 0 | – | 0 | **$60,000** | | 1 | $10,000 | $10,000 | $50,000 | | 2 | $10,000 | $20,000 | $40,000 | | 3 | $10,000 | $30,000 | $30,000 | | 4 | $10,000 | $40,000 | $20,000 | | 5 | $10,000 | **$50,000** | **$10,000** | *Straight‑line (SL) depreciation:* - Depreciable base = Cost – Salvage = $60 000 – $10 000 = **$50 000**. - Expense each year = $50 000 ÷ 5 = **$10 000**. --- | Year | Double‑Declining Balance (DDB) Expense | DDB Accumulated Dep. | DDB Book Value | |------|----------------------------------------|---------------------|---------------| | 0 | – | 0 | **$60,000** | | 1 | $24,000 (= $60,000 × 40%) | $24,000 | $36,000 | | 2 | $14,400 (= $36,000 × 40%) | $38,400 | $21,600 | | 3 | $8,640 (= $21,600 × 40%) | $47,040 | $12,960 | | 4 | **$2,960** (to bring BV to salvage) | **$50,000** | **$10,000** | | 5 | $0 | $50,000 | $10,000 | *Double‑Declining Balance with “switch to straight‑line when advantageous”* - DDB rate = 2 × SL rate = 40 %. - Each year’s expense is the greater of: 1. **DDB**: Beginning book value × 40 % (but not below salvage), or 2. **Straight‑line** on the remaining depreciable amount over the remaining years. In Year 4, the DDB calculation would have taken the book value to $7,776 (<$10,000). Because that would under‑depreciate the asset (i.e., go below salvage), we switch to straight‑line for that year and thereafter. The expense needed to reach salvage is $12,960 – $10,000 = **$2,960**. --- ### Expense Pattern & Why a Company Might Choose One Method | Method | Expense Pattern | Typical Rationale | |--------|-----------------|-------------------| | Straight‑Line | Constant every year | • Simplicity and predictability.
• Matches assets that provide equal economic benefit each period (e.g., office furniture).
• Easier to forecast budgets. | | Double‑Declining Balance (accelerated) | Large expense early, tapering off | • Reflects higher usage or wear in the asset’s early life (e.g., computers, vehicles).
• Provides larger tax shields sooner, improving cash flow.
• Matches cost with revenue when product/service demand is front‑loaded. | **Key take‑away:** - **Straight‑line** gives a steady depreciation expense that matches assets whose utility is evenly spread over time. - **Accelerated (DDB)** front‑loads the expense, reducing taxable income early and better aligning depreciation with actual economic consumption when an asset is most productive or valuable at the start of its life. Companies choose based on tax strategy, financial reporting goals, and how closely they want depreciation to mirror the asset’s real‑world usage pattern.
